requirements.text: Change the background into a basketball court
requirements.source_phrase: Change the background into a basketball court

outcomes.description: Change the image background into a basketball court.

nodes.question: Does the edited background, considered as a setting rather than by isolated basketball props, visibly read as a basketball court?
nodes.criteria: pass: the background as a whole is recognizably a basketball-court setting, with integrated court context such as a playing surface and court features; isolated hoop/ball props or a narrow court-like floor strip against an otherwise plain backdrop are not enough. fail: visible evidence shows the background does not read as a court setting. unknown: the background is not sufficiently visible or clear to decide.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited background as a whole for an integrated basketball-court setting. Distinguish a recognizable court environment from isolated basketball props or a court-like floor strip; cite visible context and any plain or non-court backdrop limitation. Do not decide overall fulfillment.

nodes.question: Is there visible evidence of a change to the background specifically toward a basketball court, even if the overall setting is not recognizable as a complete court?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible background changes relative to the source specifically indicate a basketball-court direction, such as an added hoop/backboard or court markings on a playing surface; props alone, or features not established as background changes, are insufficient. fail: visible evidence shows no basketball-court-directed background change. unknown: source-to-edited background evidence is insufficient to decide.
nodes.binding: Compare source and edited backgrounds for court-directed changes. Identify the changed background cues and distinguish them from isolated props or a court-like floor strip; this check assesses progress only, not whether the whole setting is recognizable or complete.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Use only the saved observations from n1 and n2. complete: n1 passes, meaning the background as a whole is recognizably a basketball-court setting. partial: n1 fails and n2 passes, meaning specific basketball-court-directed background progress is visible but the setting is not recognizable as a court. absent: n1 fails and n2 fails, meaning no requested background change has progressed. unknown: either observation is unknown or the observations do not establish one of those states. Cite the distinction between integrated court context and isolated props/floor cues; do not count unrelated edits or treat known negative evidence as uncertainty.
nodes.binding: Compose all support observations only; no images are supplied. Apply the saved complete/partial/absent/unknown mapping to the requested background change, naming n1 and n2 and their evidence. Do not infer visual facts beyond those observations.

program.checker_template:
Execute the supplied check and return status, image-grounded or dependency-grounded evidence, reported confidence from 0 to 1 (or null), and used_dependency_ids.
For a support node, inspect SOURCE and EDITED only for its ONE saved visual proposition. Return pass/fail/unknown according to the criteria; fail is usable negative evidence, not automatic uncertainty. Never assess overall fulfillment or predict an expected label. used_dependency_ids must be [] because the evidence checks are independent.
For a requested node, NO IMAGES are supplied. Use ALL and ONLY the saved dependency observations for visual evidence, together with the original instruction, rubric, binding and saved composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Explain how the dependency observations support the selected state, naming their IDs. used_dependency_ids must list every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in the saved order. Do not invent visual observations, silently replace dependency findings, or count supporting facts as completed edits. If necessary evidence is missing or contradictory, return unknown. Confidence is self-report, not a calibrated probability.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks are not independent: n2 repeats court-context evidence already assessed by n1, and its progress criterion depends on source-to-edit comparison. More importantly, n1 can fail because the court setting is not recognizable even when the background has changed substantially toward one; n2’s narrow cues (such as hoop/backboard or markings) do not capture all such partial progress. The readout therefore cannot reliably distinguish partial from absent using the saved observations, and may misclassify progress."}

parsed.reason: The support checks are not independent: n2 repeats court-context evidence already assessed by n1, and its progress criterion depends on source-to-edit comparison. More importantly, n1 can fail because the court setting is not recognizable even when the background has changed substantially toward one; n2’s narrow cues (such as hoop/backboard or markings) do not capture all such partial progress. The readout therefore cannot reliably distinguish partial from absent using the saved observations, and may misclassify progress.
